newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares soar to new high, further gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares soar to new high, further gains seen.

text.p: The Philippine stock index soared to a record closing high on Thursday and jubilant brokers and bourse officials said they saw further gains as the market rode the waves of a buoyant economy.

"The phenomenon that we experienced today tends to indicate that the investing community around the world is really looking at the Philippines as the looming tiger economy of Asia ... and our stock exchange as the tiger stock exchange of Asia," Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on the trading floor as champagne corks popped after the closing bell.

The stock index rallied 0.57 percent to close at 3,392.76 points in heavy volume. Blue-chip issues which registered strong earnings growth in the past year led the upsurge, taking the index briefly above 3,400 points during the day.

"What is significant about this rally was that the turnover reached more than 4.0 billion pesos ($151 million)... We're already catching up with Thailand (in terms of value turnover). We've surpassed Indonesia," Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) chairman Wilson Sy told reporters.
Brokers attributed the strong wave of buying to heightened confidence in the Philippine economy.
On Wednesday, the government said gross national product (GNP) grew by 6.8 percent last year, up from 5.5 percent in 1995. GNP is expected to rise by 7.0 to 8.0 percent this year.
"Right from the start, there was already a rally," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice president of Diversified Securities.

"I think the 4,000 index is a possibility within the year. There are a lot of new issues coming up that will help boost the market ... We can test 4,000 between the middle of the year and end of the year."
Amid the jubilation, bourse officials said continuous efforts to professionalise the market were under way, including moves to curb insider trading and price manipulation.
PSE President Vitaliano Nanagas said the exchange was studying the possibility of suspending the trading of a share if it breached daily fluctuation limits.
At present, the bourse only freezes the price of a stock which has risen 50 percent or fallen 40 percent within the trading day. The shares can still be traded within the limits.
Suspending the share would allow the bourse to investigate fully the cause of the sharp fluctuation and protect investors from possible insider trading, officials said.
